author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Move an EmuCoreX PS2 library to an SD card without losing identity
summary: Copy verified personal images to removable storage, prove every byte arrived, switch the Android document-tree grant once, and retain the internal source until titles, regions, favorites, and cold boots all match.
heroAlt: PCSX2 disc-image tool writing a verified image, illustrating the read-and-verify stage before a library move
searchKeywords: move EmuCoreX games to SD card

blocks.text: Treat the SD card as a new physical library root

Moving a PS2 library is not a rename. Android exposes the SD card through a storage provider, and the new folder receives a different document-tree URI from internal storage. EmuCoreX must be pointed at that tree only after the copy is complete. Keep BIOS files, memory cards, save states, profiles, covers, and logs in the emulator-data backup; this procedure moves only personally dumped game images.
Copy first and verify second. Do not use a file manager's Move action for the initial transfer, because a full destination or interrupted card can leave neither side as a complete reference.
Measure the source and qualify the card

items: A mounted SD card that Android can browse after a reboot.
A source inventory containing relative path, byte size, and SHA-256 for every playable image and cue/bin component.
Free card capacity greater than the total source size plus at least ten percent working margin.
A filesystem able to store the largest single PS2 image.
A separate backup of EmuCoreX saves and profiles, created while emulation is closed.

blocks.text: Copy, compare, then switch the grant

items: 1. Create one empty PS2 library folder on the SD card; do not place archives or emulator data inside it.
2. Copy a small verified title and the largest verified title first. Reopen both from the card with a file manager to expose immediate read failures.
3. Copy the remaining images in batches small enough that a failed batch can be repeated without guessing which files finished.
4. Generate destination SHA-256 values and compare them with the source inventory, including every track referenced by a cue sheet.
5. In EmuCoreX, add the SD-card library folder through Android's system picker. Select that folder itself, not one game file and not the card root.
6. Refresh once, launch the small and largest test titles, and verify their displayed serial and region.
7. Force-stop EmuCoreX, restart Android, wait for the card to mount, and cold-boot the same two games.
8. Remove the internal library grant only after every destination hash and both post-reboot launches pass.

blocks.text: Favorites and per-game profiles should be checked before the source root is retired. If EmuCoreX temporarily shows two copies, compare each entry's location instead of deleting a file. The correct sequence is destination added, destination proven, old grant removed, then source files archived or deleted later by the owner.
Acceptance evidence for the migrated root
The card is accepted only when content integrity and Android persistence both pass. A successful copy notification is not evidence of either one.

items: Source and destination inventories contain the same relative files and byte counts.
SHA-256 values match for every moved component.
The library contains no parent/child root overlap and no duplicate entry after the internal grant is removed.
One CD-based set and one DVD image cold-boot from the SD card.
The folder remains authorized after force-stop and Android restart.

blocks.text: Stop conditions during an SD-card move

items: The largest file is rejected near 4 GiB: identify the card filesystem before retrying.
Hashes differ even though sizes match: replace the destination copy; do not tune emulator settings.
The card disappears under load: check adapter, power, filesystem health, and temperature.
Entries lose favorites: confirm the destination image is the same serial and hash, not a regional duplicate.

blocks.text: Return to internal storage without a second migration

Revoke the SD-card location in EmuCoreX and rescan the original internal library before doing anything else. Keep the verified source untouched; never merge files back from an incomplete card copy. Retain both the pre-move hashes and Android's storage error so the failure can be classified as lost permission or failing media.
Removable-media behavior differs by Android vendor

Some devices delay SD-card mounting after boot or revoke provider access when a card is reformatted. Others expose the same card under a new URI after filesystem repair. Re-authorize the physical folder when the provider identity changes, but never accept an empty or cloud-placeholder tree merely because its visible name matches.
